title: General-Case Cyclic Vector Theorem: Strategy and Coverage
content:
The module header outlines the proof strategy for the **general k-fold** case of the nonderogatory cyclic vector theorem — not just the binary (p^a · q^b) case. Given M nonderogatory with $\text{minpoly}(M) = \prod_{i : \text{Fin}\,k} p_i^{e_i}$ (pairwise coprime monic irreducible prime powers), the proof constructs a cyclic vector via:

1. **Primary vector construction**: For each $i$, define the *complementary product* $F_i := \prod_{j \neq i} p_j^{e_j}$. Choose $w_i$ so that $(p_i^{e_i - 1} F_i)(M) w_i \neq 0$ (which exists because $p_i^{e_i-1} F_i$ has degree strictly below $\deg(\text{minpoly}) = n$). Set $v_i := F_i(M) w_i$. Then $p_i^{e_i}(M) v_i = 0$ and $p_i^{e_i - 1}(M) v_i \neq 0$.
2. **CRT projection step**: The candidate cyclic vector is $v := \sum_i v_i$. For an annihilator $r$ of $v$, Bezout for the coprime pair $(p_i^{e_i}, F_i)$ gives $a_i p_i^{e_i} + b_i F_i = 1$. The projection $\pi_i := (b_i F_i)(M)$ acts as identity on $v_i$ and as zero on $v_j$ ($j \neq i$), so $r(M) v_i = \pi_i(r(M) v) = 0$.
3. **Prime-power divisibility**: By `pow_irred_dvd_of_annihilated`, $p_i^{e_i} \mid r$ for every $i$. Pairwise coprimality (`Finset.prod_dvd_of_coprime`) then forces $\prod_i p_i^{e_i} = \text{minpoly} \mid r$, contradicting $\deg r < n$.

This WIP04 file is **the** completion of the family-of-cases proof: WIP02 handled the squarefree case (all exponents 1), WIP03 handled the single-prime-power case (k = 1), and WIP04 combines the two via primary decomposition with arbitrary k and arbitrary exponents. WIP01's rational canonical form axiom is eliminated entirely.
mathContext: For nonderogatory $M$ with $\text{minpoly}(M) = \prod_{i \in \text{Fin}\,k} p_i^{e_i}$ pairwise coprime: the CRT decomposition $K[X]/(\prod p_i^{e_i}) \cong \prod_i K[X]/(p_i^{e_i})$ induces a direct-sum decomposition $K^n = \bigoplus_i \ker(p_i^{e_i}(M))$. The cyclic vector $v = \sum_i v_i$ has each $v_i$ generating a *maximal* cyclic submodule of the $i$-th primary component (since $p_i^{e_i - 1}(M) v_i \neq 0$ forces the cyclic submodule generated by $v_i$ to have annihilator exactly $p_i^{e_i}$).

title: IsCyclicVector and IsNonderogatory
content:
Two definitions consistent with sibling WIP files:

- **`IsCyclicVector M v`**: no nonzero polynomial of degree $< n$ annihilates $v$ when evaluated at $M$ and applied to $v$ via `mulVec`. Equivalently, $\{v, Mv, M^2 v, \ldots, M^{n-1} v\}$ is linearly independent (and hence spans $K^n$ since $\dim K^n = n$).
- **`IsNonderogatory M`**: the minimal polynomial equals the characteristic polynomial, $\text{minpoly}_K(M) = \text{charpoly}(M)$.

The nonderogatory condition is equivalent to several familiar statements: (i) every eigenvalue has geometric multiplicity 1; (ii) $K^n$ is cyclic as a $K[X]$-module under the action $X \cdot v := M v$; (iii) $M$ is similar to the companion matrix of its characteristic polynomial (rational canonical form, single block). The proof in this file establishes (ii) directly without first establishing (iii) — sidestepping the need for the PID structure theorem.
mathContext: Cyclic vector predicate: $v$ is cyclic for $M$ iff $\forall p \in K[X],\; \deg(p) < n \wedge p(M) v = 0 \implies p = 0$. Nonderogatory predicate: $\text{minpoly}_K(M) = \text{charpoly}(M)$, which by Cayley–Hamilton and the divisibility $\text{minpoly} \mid \text{charpoly}$ is equivalent to $\deg(\text{minpoly}_K M) = n$.

title: Bezout-from-Annihilation: The Core Algebraic Lemma
content:
**`irreducible_dvd_of_annihilated`**: if $p$ is irreducible, $v \neq 0$, $p(M) v = 0$, and $r(M) v = 0$, then $p \mid r$.

The argument is a clean application of Bezout's identity in the UFD $K[X]$. If $p \nmid r$, then since $p$ is prime (using `UniqueFactorizationMonoid.irreducible_iff_prime` to lift irreducibility to primality), $p$ and $r$ are coprime: there exist $a, b \in K[X]$ with $a p + b r = 1$. Evaluating both sides at $M$ and applying to $v$:
$$v = 1 \cdot v = (a(M) p(M) + b(M) r(M)) v = a(M)(p(M) v) + b(M)(r(M) v) = a(M) \cdot 0 + b(M) \cdot 0 = 0,$$
contradicting $v \neq 0$. Hence $p \mid r$.

This lemma is the *only* step that uses irreducibility of $p$ directly. The rest of the proof — the prime-power induction `pow_irred_dvd_of_annihilated` and the CRT projection argument — bootstraps from this single Bezout fact, which is why the proof avoids the PID module structure theorem entirely.
mathContext: Bezout in $K[X]$: $\gcd(p, r) = 1 \iff \exists a, b \in K[X],\; a p + b r = 1$. For irreducible $p$, $\gcd(p, r) \in \{1, p\}$, so $p \nmid r \iff \gcd(p, r) = 1 \iff $ coprime. The contrapositive of the lemma is the standard fact: if $p$ irreducible and $p$ and $r$ have a common annihilator $v$ outside $\ker = \{0\}$, they share a common factor — but the only proper factor of $p$ is the unit, so $p \mid r$.

title: Utility Helpers: Existence, Degree Bounds, Commutativity, CRT Projection
content:
Four supporting lemmas used throughout the main proof:

1. **`exists_mulVec_ne_zero`** (lines 91–97): a nonzero matrix $A \neq 0$ has some vector $v$ with $A v \neq 0$. Proved by contradiction: if $A v = 0$ for all $v$, then evaluating at the standard basis vectors $\delta_j$ would give every column of $A$ equal to zero, hence $A = 0$.

2. **`aeval_ne_zero_of_lt_minpoly`** (lines 99–103): if $p \neq 0$ and $\deg(p) < \deg(\text{minpoly}_K M)$, then $p(M) \neq 0$ as a matrix. Equivalent to the minimality clause in the definition of minimal polynomial: any polynomial of strictly smaller degree cannot annihilate $M$. Used to guarantee that $(p_i^{e_i-1} F_i)(M)$ is nonzero, so the choice of witness $w_i$ in the main proof is well-defined.

3. **`aeval_mul_comm`** (lines 105–108): polynomial evaluations at the same matrix commute, $f(M) g(M) = g(M) f(M)$. This follows from $K[X]$ being commutative and the evaluation map `aeval M` being a ring homomorphism — but it is invoked dozens of times in the main proof, so factoring it out as a named lemma keeps the main argument readable.

4. **`bezout_proj_identity`** (lines 110–120): the CRT projection identity. If $a p + b q = 1$ and $p(M) v = 0$, then $(b q)(M) v = v$. Geometrically: in the CRT decomposition $K[X]/(pq) \cong K[X]/(p) \times K[X]/(q)$, the projection $b q \bmod pq$ is the idempotent that picks out the $K[X]/(p)$ summand. The proof multiplies the Bezout identity by $v$, kills the $a p$ term using $p(M) v = 0$, and reads off the result.

A companion 'kills-the-other-summand' lemma is not factored out separately because in the main proof, $F_i$ kills $v_j$ for $j \neq i$ via direct divisibility ($p_j^{e_j} \mid F_i$) rather than via the Bezout identity.
mathContext: Together these helpers handle: existence of non-killed vectors, the minimality clause of minpoly, ring-hom commutativity of evaluation, and the idempotent projection from Bezout. The CRT projection is the $K[X]$-module analogue of the Chinese Remainder Theorem isomorphism $K[X]/(pq) \cong K[X]/(p) \times K[X]/(q)$, where $b q + (pq) \in K[X]/(pq)$ is the idempotent corresponding to $(0, 1)$ in the product.

title: Prime Power Divisibility from Annihilation: The Inductive Lemma
content:
**`pow_irred_dvd_of_annihilated`**: if $p$ is irreducible, $p^e(M) v \neq 0$, $p^{e+1}(M) v = 0$, and $r(M) v = 0$, then $p^{e+1} \mid r$.

The induction is on $e$. 

- **Base case ($e = 0$)**: $v \neq 0$ (since $p^0(M) v = v \neq 0$), $p(M) v = 0$, $r(M) v = 0$. Direct application of `irreducible_dvd_of_annihilated` gives $p \mid r$, which is $p^1 \mid r$.

- **Inductive step ($e \to e+1$)**: assume $p^{e+1}(M) v \neq 0$, $p^{e+2}(M) v = 0$, $r(M) v = 0$.

  - *Step 1 (extract one factor of $p$ from $r$)*: set $w := p^{e+1}(M) v$. Then $p(M) w = p^{e+2}(M) v = 0$ and $r(M) w = (r \cdot p^{e+1})(M) v = (p^{e+1} \cdot r)(M) v = p^{e+1}(M) (r(M) v) = 0$ (using $r(M) v = 0$ and the commutativity of polynomial evaluations). Apply `irreducible_dvd_of_annihilated` to $p, r, w$: $p \mid r$, so $r = p \cdot r_1$ for some $r_1$.
  - *Step 2 (apply IH at the next level)*: set $u := p(M) v$. Verify $p^e(M) u = p^{e+1}(M) v \neq 0$ and $p^{e+1}(M) u = p^{e+2}(M) v = 0$. Need $r_1(M) u = 0$: compute $r_1(M)(p(M) v) = (r_1 \cdot p)(M) v = (p \cdot r_1)(M) v = r(M) v = 0$. By IH applied at exponent $e$ to $u$ and polynomial $r_1$: $p^{e+1} \mid r_1$, so $r_1 = p^{e+1} \cdot r_2$. Therefore $r = p \cdot r_1 = p \cdot p^{e+1} \cdot r_2 = p^{e+2} \cdot r_2$, giving $p^{e+2} \mid r$.

This lemma is the inductive heart that lifts the base-case Bezout argument to arbitrary exponents and is the substitute for the primary decomposition step in the PID structure theorem. Each inductive layer 'peels off' one factor of $p$ from $r$ by shifting the witness from level $e+1$ down to level $e$ via the action of $p(M)$.
mathContext: The induction structurally mimics the primary decomposition $\ker(p^{e+1}(M)) / \ker(p^e(M)) \cong K[X]/(p)$ in the PID-module picture, but proceeds entirely at the level of polynomial divisibility — no submodule quotients are constructed, no dimensions counted. This is what makes the proof work over arbitrary fields including small finite fields where dimension-counting + union-avoidance arguments fail.

title: mulVec Distributes Over Finite Sums
content:
**`mulVec_finset_sum`**: $A \cdot (\sum_{i \in s} f_i) = \sum_{i \in s} A \cdot f_i$ for a matrix $A$ and a finite indexed family of vectors. Proved by induction on the finset using `Finset.induction_on` and `Matrix.mulVec_add`.

This is the key linearity fact that makes the candidate cyclic vector $v = \sum_i v_i$ tractable in the main proof: an annihilator $r$ satisfies $r(M) v = \sum_i r(M) v_i$, which is what allows the CRT projection to extract each $r(M) v_i = 0$ separately.
mathContext: Linearity of `mulVec` in the vector argument: $A : K^n \to K^n$ is $K$-linear, so it commutes with finite sums. Mathlib has this for `Finset.sum` via the standard induction pattern.

title: Main Theorem: nonderogatory_general_has_cyclic_vector
content:
The main theorem states: for any field $K$, any nonderogatory matrix $M : \text{Matrix}\,(\text{Fin}\,n)\,(\text{Fin}\,n)\,K$ with $\text{minpoly}_K(M) = \prod_{i : \text{Fin}\,k} p_i^{e_i}$ (pairwise coprime, $p_i$ monic irreducible, $e_i \geq 1$, $k \geq 1$), there exists $v$ with `IsCyclicVector M v`.

The proof has six phases:

1. **Edge case $n = 0$**: the only function $\text{Fin}\,0 \to K$ is the empty function `Fin.elim0`, which is trivially cyclic.

2. **Degree of minpoly**: from $h\_nd$ and `Matrix.charpoly_natDegree_eq_dim` plus `Fintype.card_fin`, derive $\deg(\text{minpoly}_K M) = n$.

3. **Complementary product setup**: define $F : \text{Fin}\,k \to K[X]$ by $F_i := \prod_{j \in \text{univ.erase}\,i} p_j^{e_j}$. Establish $F_i \neq 0$ (each factor is nonzero) and $p_i^{e_i} \cdot F_i = \text{minpoly}\,K\,M$ via `Finset.mul_prod_erase`.

4. **Primary vector construction**: bound $\deg(p_i^{e_i - 1} \cdot F_i) < n$ (using `Polynomial.natDegree_mul`, the multiplicative identity $(p_i^{e_i-1} F_i) \cdot p_i = p_i^{e_i} F_i = \text{minpoly}$, and `omega`). Apply `aeval_ne_zero_of_lt_minpoly` to get $(p_i^{e_i-1} F_i)(M) \neq 0$. Use `exists_mulVec_ne_zero` to choose $w_i$ with $(p_i^{e_i-1} F_i)(M) w_i \neq 0$. Set $v_i := F_i(M) w_i$. Then $p_i^{e_i}(M) v_i = 0$ (since $p_i^{e_i} \cdot F_i = \text{minpoly}$ and `minpoly.aeval` gives $\text{minpoly}(M) = 0$) and $p_i^{e_i - 1}(M) v_i \neq 0$ (by choice of $w_i$).

5. **CRT extraction**: candidate cyclic vector $v := \sum_i v_i$. Suppose $r(M) v = 0$ with $\deg(r) < n$, aiming for $r = 0$. For each $i$, Bezout for $(p_i^{e_i}, F_i)$ (proved coprime via `IsCoprime.prod_right` from the input pairwise coprimality) gives $a_i p_i^{e_i} + b_i F_i = 1$. The projection $\pi_i = (b_i F_i)(M)$:
   - acts as identity on $v_i$: by `bezout_proj_identity` since $p_i^{e_i}(M) v_i = 0$;
   - kills $v_j$ for $j \neq i$: since $p_j^{e_j} \mid F_i$ (direct fact from `Finset.dvd_prod_of_mem`), we factor $F_i = p_j^{e_j} \cdot Q$, commute via `aeval_mul_comm`, and kill via $p_j^{e_j}(M) v_j = 0$.

   Apply $\pi_i$ to both sides of $r(M) v = 0$, use commutativity of polynomial evaluations to swap $\pi_i$ past $r(M)$, and read off $r(M) v_i = 0$.

6. **Divisibility and degree contradiction**: by `pow_irred_dvd_of_annihilated` applied with the witness $v_i$ (which has $p_i^{e_i-1}(M) v_i \neq 0$ and $p_i^{e_i}(M) v_i = 0$), each $p_i^{e_i} \mid r$. By `Finset.prod_dvd_of_coprime`, $\prod_i p_i^{e_i} \mid r$. Since $\prod_i p_i^{e_i} = \text{minpoly}\,K\,M$ has degree $n$, `Polynomial.natDegree_le_of_dvd` (assuming $r \neq 0$ for contradiction) gives $\deg r \geq n$, contradicting $\deg r < n$.

The whole proof is purely algebraic — no dimension counting, no submodule quotients, no field-size hypothesis — which is why it works over any field including $\mathbb{F}_2$.
mathContext: Key formal ingredients: $\text{IsCoprime}$ in $K[X]$ (Bezout coefficients), $\text{Finset.prod\_dvd\_of\_coprime}$ (extracting product divisibility from pairwise coprimality), `Polynomial.natDegree_le_of_dvd` (the degree-bound contradiction), and `aeval_mul_comm` (commutativity of polynomial evaluations at $M$, used to slide $\pi_i$ past $r(M)$ in the CRT extraction). The non-triviality of $r$ (assumed for contradiction) is the only place `by_contra` enters.

title: Commentary: Path to Unconditional Theorem and Why No Dimension Argument is Needed
content:
The closing commentary records three observations:

1. **Path to the unconditional theorem**: the only remaining hypothesis is the *factored form* of $\text{minpoly}_K M$. To eliminate it, factor the minimal polynomial using $K[X]$ as a UFD via Mathlib's `UniqueFactorizationMonoid` instance, producing data $(k, p_i, e_i)$ that satisfies all the input hypotheses, and apply `nonderogatory_general_has_cyclic_vector`. This is purely a Mathlib API exercise — no new mathematical content is required.

2. **No dimension argument is needed**: the proof never establishes $\dim \ker(p_i^{e_i}(M)) = \deg(p_i^{e_i})$ or any other dimension equality. Only the annihilation/non-annihilation properties of the primary vectors $v_i$ are used. This is the structural reason the proof works over arbitrary fields including $\mathbb{F}_2, \mathbb{F}_3, \ldots$ without any field-size or 'enough vectors' hypothesis. Classical proofs that route through union-avoidance ('the set of non-cyclic vectors is a union of $\leq n$ proper subspaces, so some vector escapes when $|K| > n$') are sharp for infinite fields but break for $\mathbb{F}_q$ with $q \leq n$.

3. **Supersedes WIP01**: WIP01 used a single axiom — `nonderogatory_similar_to_companion`, equivalent to rational canonical form — to discharge the case where $\text{minpoly}_K M$ has multiple distinct prime factors. WIP04 eliminates the axiom entirely. The technique (primary vectors via complementary products, CRT projections, prime-power divisibility induction) could plausibly be ported to Mathlib as a lemma about cyclic $K[X]$-modules without first formalizing the full PID structure theorem — a substantial Mathlib gap as of version 4.26.

Together with WIP02 (squarefree case, all exponents 1) and WIP03 (single-prime-power case, $k = 1$), WIP04 closes the family-of-cases proof of the nonderogatory cyclic vector theorem. The next step in the dependency chain is OQ-05-OQ-01-OQ-04 (the parent), which combines WIP04 with K[X]-UFD factorization to obtain the unconditional theorem.
mathContext: The unconditional theorem schema: given $M$ nonderogatory, $\text{minpoly}_K M$ is a polynomial in the UFD $K[X]$, hence factors as $\prod_i p_i^{e_i}$ with $p_i$ monic irreducible. The factorization is unique up to permutation, and the input data $(p, e, \text{hp\_irr}, \text{hp\_monic}, \text{he\_pos}, \text{hcoprime}, \text{hprod})$ to `nonderogatory_general_has_cyclic_vector` is exactly the data of such a factorization. The 'separate (open) step' mentioned in `meta.assumptions` is producing this data from `IsNonderogatory M` automatically, which requires Mathlib glue rather than new mathematics.
